definition: Frank Rosenblatt (July 11, 1928 – July 11, 1971) was an American psychologist notable in the field of artificial intelligence.
details: Built the Mark I Perceptron in 1957, the first hardware artificial neural network capable of learning via weight adjustments. He is sometimes called the father of deep learning for his pioneering work on artificial neural networks.

explainer.lead: Frank Rosenblatt was an American psychologist (1928–1971).
explainer.knownFor: === Perceptron === Rosenblatt is best known for the Perceptron, an electronic device which was constructed in accordance with biological principles and showed an ability to learn.

contributions.name: He developed and extended this approach in many papers and a book called Principles of Neurodynamics: Perceptrons and the Theory of Brain Mechanisms, published by Spartan Books in 1962.

timeline.what: He used it between 1951 and 1953 to analyze psychometric data collected for his PhD thesis.
Rosenblatt's perceptrons were initially simulated on an IBM 704 computer at Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory in 1957.
George Nagy received a PhD in 1962 under Rosenblatt, primarily for work on Tobermory.
Frank Rosenblatt died in July 1971 on his 43rd birthday, in a boating accident in Chesapeake Bay.
